label: Luke 2:1
text: Now in those days, a decree went out from Caesar Augustus that all the world should be enrolled.

label: Luke 2:2
text: This was the first enrollment made when Quirinius was governor of Syria.

label: Luke 2:3
text: All went to enroll themselves, everyone to his own city.

label: Luke 2:4
text: Joseph also went up from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, into Judea, to David’s city, which is called Bethlehem, because he was of the house and family of David;

label: Luke 2:5
text: to enroll himself with Mary, who was pledged to be married to him as wife, being pregnant.

label: Luke 2:6
text: While they were there, the day had come for her to give birth.

label: Luke 2:7
text: She gave birth to her firstborn son. She wrapped him in bands of cloth, and laid him in a feeding trough, because there was no room for them in the inn.

label: Luke 2:8
text: There were shepherds in the same country staying in the field, and keeping watch by night over their flock.

label: Luke 2:9
text: Behold, an angel of the Lord stood by them, and the glory of the Lord shone around them, and they were terrified.

label: Luke 2:10
text: The angel said to them, “Don’t be afraid, for behold, I bring you good news of great joy which will be to all the people.

label: Luke 2:11
text: For there is born to you today, in David’s city, a Savior, who is Christ the Lord.

label: Luke 2:12
text: This is the sign to you: you will find a baby wrapped in strips of cloth, lying in a feeding trough.”

label: Luke 2:13
text: Suddenly, there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly army praising God, and saying,

label: Luke 2:14
text:
“Glory to God in the highest,
on earth peace, good will toward men.”

variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke' (Luke 2:14) lists εὐδοκίας ('of good will' or 'of favour' - genitive) for the Alexandrian text-type (Sinaiticus and Vaticanus among its witnesses), against εὐδοκία (nominative) in the Byzantine text-type. The WEB's 'good will toward men' follows the Byzantine reading.

label: Luke 2:15
text: When the angels went away from them into the sky, the shepherds said to one another, “Let’s go to Bethlehem, now, and see this thing that has happened, which the Lord has made known to us.”

label: Luke 2:16
text: They came with haste, and found both Mary and Joseph, and the baby was lying in the feeding trough.

label: Luke 2:17
text: When they saw it, they publicized widely the saying which was spoken to them about this child.

label: Luke 2:18
text: All who heard it wondered at the things which were spoken to them by the shepherds.

label: Luke 2:19
text: But Mary kept all these sayings, pondering them in her heart.

label: Luke 2:20
text: The shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for all the things that they had heard and seen, just as it was told them.

label: Luke 2:21
text: When eight days were fulfilled for the circumcision of the child, his name was called Jesus, which was given by the angel before he was conceived in the womb.

label: Luke 2:22
text: When the days of their purification according to the law of Moses were fulfilled, they brought him up to Jerusalem, to present him to the Lord

label: Luke 2:23
text: (as it is written in the law of the Lord, “Every male who opens the womb shall be called holy to the Lord”),

label: Luke 2:24
text: and to offer a sacrifice according to that which is said in the law of the Lord, “A pair of turtledoves, or two young pigeons.”

label: Luke 2:25
text: Behold, there was a man in Jerusalem whose name was Simeon. This man was righteous and devout, looking for the consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit was on him.

label: Luke 2:26
text: It had been revealed to him by the Holy Spirit that he should not see death before he had seen the Lord’s Christ.

label: Luke 2:27
text: He came in the Spirit into the temple. When the parents brought in the child, Jesus, that they might do concerning him according to the custom of the law,

label: Luke 2:28
text: then he received him into his arms, and blessed God, and said,

label: Luke 2:29
text:
“Now you are releasing your servant, Master,
according to your word, in peace;

label: Luke 2:30
text: for my eyes have seen your salvation,

label: Luke 2:31
text: which you have prepared before the face of all peoples;

label: Luke 2:32
text:
a light for revelation to the nations,
and the glory of your people Israel.”

label: Luke 2:33
text: Joseph and his mother were marveling at the things which were spoken concerning him,

label: Luke 2:34
text: and Simeon blessed them, and said to Mary, his mother, “Behold, this child is set for the falling and the rising of many in Israel, and for a sign which is spoken against.

label: Luke 2:35
text: Yes, a sword will pierce through your own soul, that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed.”

label: Luke 2:36
text: There was one Anna, a prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher (she was of a great age, having lived with a husband seven years from her virginity,

label: Luke 2:37
text: and she had been a widow for about eighty-four years), who didn’t depart from the temple, worshiping with fastings and petitions night and day.

label: Luke 2:38
text: Coming up at that very hour, she gave thanks to the Lord, and spoke of him to all those who were looking for redemption in Jerusalem.

label: Luke 2:39
text: When they had accomplished all things that were according to the law of the Lord, they returned into Galilee, to their own city, Nazareth.

label: Luke 2:40
text: The child was growing, and was becoming strong in spirit, being filled with wisdom, and the grace of God was upon him.

label: Luke 2:41
text: His parents went every year to Jerusalem at the feast of the Passover.

label: Luke 2:42
text: When he was twelve years old, they went up to Jerusalem according to the custom of the feast,

label: Luke 2:43
text: and when they had fulfilled the days, as they were returning, the boy Jesus stayed behind in Jerusalem. Joseph and his mother didn’t know it,

label: Luke 2:44
text: but supposing him to be in the company, they went a day’s journey, and they looked for him among their relatives and acquaintances.

label: Luke 2:45
text: When they didn’t find him, they returned to Jerusalem, looking for him.

label: Luke 2:46
text: After three days they found him in the temple, sitting in the middle of the teachers, both listening to them, and asking them questions.

label: Luke 2:47
text: All who heard him were amazed at his understanding and his answers.

label: Luke 2:48
text: When they saw him, they were astonished, and his mother said to him, “Son, why have you treated us this way? Behold, your father and I were anxiously looking for you.”

label: Luke 2:49
text:
He said to them,
“Why were you looking for me? Didn’t you know that I must be in my Father’s house?”

label: Luke 2:50
text: They didn’t understand the saying which he spoke to them.

label: Luke 2:51
text: And he went down with them, and came to Nazareth. He was subject to them, and his mother kept all these sayings in her heart.

label: Luke 2:52
text: And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and men.

label: Wikipedia: Census of Quirinius (the 6 CE census)
title: Census of Quirinius
excerpt: The Census of Quirinius was a census of the Roman province of Judaea taken in 6 CE, upon its formation, by the governor of Roman Syria, Publius Sulpicius Quirinius. The census triggered a revolt of Jewish extremists (called Zealots) led by Judas of Galilee.

label: Wikipedia: Census of Quirinius (the Luke 2 chronology problem)
title: Census of Quirinius
excerpt: The Gospel of Luke uses the Census of Quirinius to date the birth of Jesus but also cites the time of Herod the Great (who died between 5 BCE and 1 CE), while the Gospel of Matthew only references Herod the Great. Most critical scholars agree that Luke is in error.

label: Wikipedia: Census of Quirinius (no single empire-wide census)
title: Census of Quirinius
excerpt: Scholars point out that there was no single census of the entire Roman Empire under Augustus and the Romans did not directly tax client kingdoms; further, no Roman census required that people travel from their own homes to those of their ancestors.

label: Wikipedia: Quirinius (governor of Syria, 6 CE)
title: Quirinius
excerpt: After the banishment of the ethnarch Herod Archelaus from the tetrarchy of Judea in AD 6, Quirinius was appointed legate governor of Syria, to which the province of Judaea had been added for census purposes.

label: Wikipedia: Quirinius (Stele of Quintus Aemilius Secundus, census of Apamea)
title: Quirinius
excerpt: The stele commemorates a Roman officer who had served under Quirinius, stating, among other achievements: "By order of the same Quirinius I took a census of the city of Apamea".

label: Wikipedia: Quirinius (Syrian coins, year 36 of Caesar)
title: Quirinius
excerpt: Quirinius's position as governor of Syria has been validated by the discovery of coins issued by his administration there, inscribed with "the 36th year of Caesar [Augustus]" (5/6 AD counted from the Battle of Actium).

label: Wikipedia: List of Roman governors of Syria (Lapis Tiburtinus footnote)
title: List of Roman governors of Syria
excerpt: Piso was Proconsul of Asia, and received honors for defeating the Bessi. A minority theory posits that it was Publius Sulpicius Quirinius, who was in the region at the time, received honors for defeating the Homana and was the rector to Gaius Caesar.

label: Wikipedia: List of Roman governors of Syria (Quirinius 6-12 CE)
title: List of Roman governors of Syria
excerpt: 4 - 5 Lucius Volusius Saturninus 6 - 12 Publius Sulpicius Quirinius 12 - 17 Quintus Caecilius Metellus Creticus Silanus

label: Wikisource: Res Gestae Divi Augusti, chapter 8
title: The Deeds of the Divine Augustus (Res Gestae Divi Augusti)
excerpt: in my sixth consulate [28 B.C.E.] I made a census of the people with Marcus Agrippa as my colleague. I conducted a lustrum, after a forty-one year gap, in which lustrum were counted 4,063,000 heads of Roman citizens.

label: Wikisource: Josephus, Antiquities 1.192 (eighth-day circumcision)
title: The Antiquities of the Jews, Book I (Whiston)
excerpt: he charged him, in order to keep his posterity unmixed with others, that they should be circumcised in the flesh of their foreskin, and that this should be done on the eighth day after they were born

label: Wikipedia: Luke 2 (kataluma may mean guest room)
title: Luke 2
excerpt: "The inn" is translated from the Greek word κατάλυμα, kataluma, which may is "flexible" in its use. It may mean "guest room".

statement: Caesar Augustus issued a decree that the inhabited world be enrolled (registered).
label: Augustus decreed an enrollment of the world

statement: The enrollment was made while Quirinius was governor of Syria, at the time of Jesus's birth (Luke 1:5 places the annunciation in the days of Herod, king of Judea).
label: Enrollment dated to Quirinius's governorship at the birth

statement: The enrollment required everyone to go to his own city to be registered.
label: Everyone enrolled in his own city

statement: Joseph went up from Nazareth in Galilee to Bethlehem in Judea, David's city, because he was of the house and family of David, to enroll with Mary, who was pregnant.
label: Joseph went from Nazareth to Bethlehem for the enrollment

statement: The newborn was wrapped in bands of cloth and laid in a feeding trough (phatne) because there was no room for them in the lodging (kataluma).
label: No room in the kataluma; the child laid in a manger

statement: Shepherds were staying in the fields near Bethlehem, keeping watch by night over their flock.
label: Shepherds keeping watch by night

statement: Jesus was circumcised on the eighth day after his birth, as the law required.
label: Circumcision on the eighth day

statement: After the days of purification the parents brought Jesus to Jerusalem to present him to the Lord and offered a sacrifice of a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.
label: Purification sacrifice of two turtledoves or pigeons

statement: Simeon, a righteous and devout man in Jerusalem who was looking for the consolation of Israel, received the infant Jesus in his arms in the temple and blessed him.
label: Simeon received the child in the temple

statement: Anna, a prophetess, daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher, an aged widow who worshiped in the temple night and day, gave thanks and spoke of Jesus to those looking for redemption in Jerusalem.
label: Anna the prophetess spoke of the child

statement: When they had accomplished all things required by the law of the Lord, the family returned to Galilee, to their own city Nazareth.
label: The family returned to Nazareth after the purification

statement: Jesus's parents went up to Jerusalem every year for the feast of the Passover, and Jesus went with them at the age of twelve.
label: Annual Passover pilgrimage to Jerusalem

statement: After three days Jesus was found in the temple courts sitting among the teachers (didaskaloi), listening to them and asking them questions.
label: Jesus among the teachers in the temple
